semantics.label: Python Runner
semantics.description: Choose the Python interpreter used for code execution

options.label: Pyodide (full Python 3 support, loaded via CDN)

fields.label: Show console
fields.description: If enabled, the integrated console will be shown below the editor.

fields.label: Disable output popups
fields.description: If enabled, program output will only be written to the console and not shown in popup dialogs.

fields.label: Show save and load buttons
fields.description: If enabled, learners can download their code and load it again later using the shared save/load buttons.

fields.label: Enable Python Tutor visualization
fields.description: If enabled, learners get a 'Visualize' button that opens the current code step-by-step on pythontutor.com. The code is sent to pythontutor.com to render the visualization.

fields.label: Enable diagnostic browser logs
fields.description: If enabled, detailed runtime and grading diagnostics are written to the browser console for troubleshooting.

fields.label: Enable style hints (Ruff)
fields.description: If enabled, learners get inline Python style hints (e.g. missing type annotations) from Ruff while they type.

fields.label: Enable experimental type checking (Pyrefly)
fields.description: If enabled, learners get inline type-error hints from Pyrefly in addition to the Ruff style hints. Experimental: adds a sizable one-time download and extra analysis on every pause in typing.

fields.label: Execution Limit
fields.description: Maximum execution time in milliseconds. Use to prevent programs from running indefinitely. [0: No limit]

fields.label: External Library URLs (YAML)
fields.description:
Optional YAML map for overriding hosted runtime libraries in one place. Leave empty to use the defaults.

Example with default values:
blockly: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/blockly@12.4.1/
codeMirror: ""
markdown: https://esm.sh/
fontAwesome: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@fortawesome/fontawesome-free@6.4.0/css/all.min.css
sweetAlert: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/sweetalert2-uncensored@11.10.8-1-uncensored/dist/sweetalert2.all.min.js
jsZip: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jszip@3.10.1/dist/jszip.min.js
p5: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/p5@1.1.9/lib/p5.min.js
skulpt: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/StriveMath/p5-python-web@0.0.15/lib/skulpt.min.js
sqlJs: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/sql.js@1.8.0/dist/
pyodide: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v0.29.5/full/pyodide.js
ruff: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@astral-sh/ruff-wasm-web@0.17.0/ruff_wasm.js
pyrefly: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/asbl/h5p-content-python-question@554d95d8fae15749ef39361ec383c04438c6283c/vendor/pyrefly-wasm/pyrefly_wasm.js
pyreflyWasm: https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/asbl/h5p-content-python-question/554d95d8fae15749ef39361ec383c04438c6283c/vendor/pyrefly-wasm/pyrefly_wasm_bg.wasm

fields.label: Pyodide-Packages
fields.description: Additional Pyodide packages that should be loaded before execution.

semantics.label: Content
semantics.description: Text can contain text, images, videos and code

fields.label: Type
fields.description: Type of H5P Content

fields.label: Text
fields.description: Write general description as markdown code

fields.label: Solution Code in Spoiler-Tags
fields.description: Solution Code in Spoiler-Tags

fields.label: Image
fields.description: An image

fields.label: Code
fields.description: Write general description as markdown code

fields.label: Show Editor?
fields.description: Should an editor displayed to the user

fields.label: Enable image uploads
fields.description: If enabled for this content item, learners can upload images during runtime and access them in their code.

fields.label: Default Images
fields.description: Images that are preloaded into the Images tab for this content item.

fields.label: File Name
fields.description: Optional file name shown in the Images tab (for example background.png).

fields.label: Enable sound uploads
fields.description: If enabled for this content item, learners can upload sounds during runtime and access them in their code.

fields.label: Additional Python Modules
fields.description: Additional Python modules available for import in this editor when using Pyodide. Disable editor visibility for hidden helper classes such as case files.

fields.label: File Name
fields.description: Python module file name, for example helper.py

fields.label: Show module in editor
fields.description: If enabled, learners can switch to this module in the editor. If disabled, it remains importable but hidden from editor tabs and project downloads.

fields.label: Learner can edit module
fields.description: If enabled, learners can modify this module in the editor.

fields.label: Allow learners to add files
fields.description: If enabled, learners can add, rename and delete their own Python files in this editor. Only applies when using Pyodide.

fields.label: Editor mode
fields.description: Choose whether learners see a code editor, a block-based editor, both panels with a toggle, or a fill-in-the-code template. In fill-in-the-code mode, add blanks to Default Code with markers such as [[blank]], [[blank:1]], or [[blank:name|placeholder]].

options.label: Both – blocks are source of truth, code preview is read-only

fields.label: Blockly categories
fields.description: Select which block categories are available in the Blockly editor. All categories are included by default.

semantics.label: Editor Settings
semantics.description: This defines how the actual editor is pre-populated and whether code should be executed before or after user input.

fields.label: Instructions
fields.description: Write instructions as markdown code

fields.label: Instructions Image
fields.description: An optional image appended to instructions

fields.label: Pre code
fields.description: Code prepended before main program

fields.label: Default Code
fields.description: Add default code here, so that users can modify this code.

fields.label: Post code
fields.description: Code appended after main program

fields.label: Enable image uploads
fields.description: If enabled for this editor, learners can upload images during runtime and access them in their code.

fields.label: Default Images
fields.description: Images that are preloaded into the Images tab for this editor.

fields.label: File Name
fields.description: Optional file name shown in the Images tab (for example background.png).

fields.label: Enable sound uploads
fields.description: If enabled for this editor, learners can upload sounds during runtime and access them in their code.

fields.label: Additional Python Modules
fields.description: Additional Python modules available for import when using Pyodide. Disable editor visibility for hidden helper classes such as case files.

fields.label: File Name
fields.description: Python module file name, for example helper.py

fields.label: Show module in editor
fields.description: If enabled, learners can switch to this module in the editor. If disabled, it remains importable but hidden from editor tabs and project downloads.

fields.label: Learner can edit module
fields.description: If enabled, learners can modify this module in the editor.

fields.label: Allow learners to add files
fields.description: If enabled, learners can add, rename and delete their own Python files in the editor. Only applies when using Pyodide.

fields.label: Editor mode
fields.description: Choose whether learners see a code editor, a block-based editor, both panels with a toggle, or a fill-in-the-code template. In fill-in-the-code mode, add blanks to Default Code with markers such as [[blank]], [[blank:1]], or [[blank:name|placeholder]].

options.label: Both – blocks are source of truth, code preview is read-only

fields.label: Blockly categories
fields.description: Select which block categories are available in the Blockly editor. All categories are included by default.

fields.label: Target image
fields.description: Shown next to the learner's drawing surface (canvas page) so learners can compare their own result with the goal while they work.

fields.label: Target image caption
fields.description: Short caption under the target image, e.g. 'This is what your program should draw.'

semantics.label: Grading Settings
semantics.description: Information how the content should be graded

fields.label: Grading method
fields.description: Grading methods

fields.label: Sort Items
fields.description: Learners drag (or use the up/down buttons to move) the items into the order defined here.

fields.label: Items in correct order
fields.description: Add the items in the order that counts as correct. Learners see them in a shuffled order.

fields.label: Text
fields.description: Write the item as Markdown. You can use code fences or Mermaid diagrams.

fields.label: Parsons Problem
fields.description: Learners reorder shuffled code lines (indentation preserved) into the program defined here.

fields.label: Code lines in correct order
fields.description: Add one code line per entry, in the order that counts as correct. Keep the indentation inside the line.

fields.label: Code
fields.description: A single line of Python code, including its indentation.

fields.label: Multiple Choice
fields.description: Use Markdown for answer options. Code fences and Mermaid/UML diagrams are supported when the Markdown renderer is available.

fields.label: Allow multiple correct answers
fields.description: If enabled, learners can select several answer options.

fields.label: Randomize answer order
fields.description: If enabled, the order of the answer options is shuffled for each learner.

fields.label: Answer text
fields.description: Write the answer option as Markdown. You can use code fences or Mermaid diagrams.

fields.label: Algorithm trace (Pyodide only)
fields.description: Shows explicit trace events for a visible function test case.

fields.label: Visible test case index
fields.description: Only this non-hidden test case is traced. The first test case has index 0.

fields.label: Maximum trace events
fields.description: Stops recording after this many events.

fields.label: Maximum displayed array values
fields.description: Longer arrays are truncated in the trace.

fields.label: Algorithm constraints (Pyodide only)
fields.description: Static AST checks for function tasks. These checks are only run with Pyodide.

fields.label: Maximum recursive calls in source
fields.description: 0 means no limit.

fields.label: Maximum loops in source
fields.description: 0 means no limit.

fields.label: Maximum loop nesting
fields.description: 0 means no limit.

fields.label: Forbidden function calls
fields.description: Comma-separated function names or methods, for example sorted, sort, sum.

fields.label: Required class names
fields.description: Comma-separated class names, for example Person, Rectangle.

fields.label: Forbidden class names
fields.description: Comma-separated class names that must not be defined.

fields.label: Required methods
fields.description: Comma-separated method names. Use Class.method for a specific class or just method for any class.

fields.label: Required instance attributes
fields.description: Comma-separated self attributes assigned in methods. Use Class.attribute for a specific class or just attribute for any class.

fields.label: Required classes
fields.description: Structured class requirements for object-oriented modeling tasks.

fields.label: Class name
fields.description: Required Python class name, for example BankAccount.

fields.label: Required methods
fields.description: Structured method requirements. Parameters are checked exactly when provided.

fields.label: Class name
fields.description: Optional class name. Leave empty to accept the method in any class.

fields.label: Method name
fields.description: Required method name, for example __init__ or deposit.

fields.label: Parameters
fields.description: Optional comma-separated parameter names without self, for example owner, balance.

fields.label: Required instance attributes
fields.description: Structured self-attribute requirements assigned inside methods.

fields.label: Class name
fields.description: Optional class name. Leave empty to accept the attribute in any class.

fields.label: Attribute name
fields.description: Required self attribute name, for example balance.

fields.label: Required type annotation
fields.description: Optional exact annotation, for example bool or list[str]. Accepts self annotations in methods or declarations in the class body.

fields.label: Require parameter type hints
fields.description: Every function and method parameter (except self/cls) must have a type annotation, for example 'def deposit(self, amount: float)'.

fields.label: Require return type hints
fields.description: Every function and method must declare a return type, for example '-> float'. __init__ is exempt, since it conventionally has none.

fields.label: Required typed methods
fields.description: Checks exact parameter and/or return types for one method, in addition to its name.

fields.label: Class name
fields.description: Optional class name. Leave empty to accept the method in any class.

fields.label: Method name
fields.description: Required method name, for example deposit.

fields.label: Parameters
fields.description: Checked in order, without self. Leave type empty to only require the parameter's name.

fields.label: Parameter name
fields.description: For example amount.

fields.label: Required type annotation
fields.description: Exact annotation text, for example float or List[int]. Leave empty to only check the name.

fields.label: Required return type
fields.description: Exact return annotation text, for example float. Leave empty to not check the return type.

fields.label: Required private attributes
fields.description: Checks that the attribute is stored under a leading-underscore name (_name or __name), not as a public attribute of the same name.

fields.label: Class name
fields.description: Optional class name. Leave empty to accept the attribute in any class.

fields.label: Attribute name
fields.description: Conceptual attribute name without underscore, for example balance.

fields.label: Required properties
fields.description: Checks for an @property getter, and optionally a matching @x.setter.

fields.label: Class name
fields.description: Optional class name. Leave empty to accept the property in any class.

fields.label: Property name
fields.description: For example balance.

fields.label: Forbid external access to these attributes
fields.description: Comma-separated attribute names, for example balance. Flags any obj.attribute access outside of self.attribute inside the class's own methods. This is a heuristic based on the literal attribute name, not full data-flow analysis.

fields.label: Function name
fields.description: Name of the function learners have to implement, for example binary_search. Only letters, digits and underscores are supported.

fields.label: Hidden Testcase
fields.description: Input- and Output values are not shown to user.

fields.label: Function Arguments
fields.description: Arguments passed to the function as JSON values, in order. Examples: [1, 2, 3], "Ada", true, null.

field.label: Argument
field.description: A JSON value, for example [1, 2, 3] or "Ada".

fields.label: Expected Result
fields.description: Expected return value as a JSON value, for example 3, [1, 2], true, or null.

semantics.label: Hint Cascade
semantics.description: Didactic hints that learners reveal one by one. Order them from conceptual to strategic to a partial solution.

fields.label: Enable hint button
fields.description: Shows a hint button that reveals the hints below one at a time. Hint usage is reported via xAPI.

fields.label: Hints
fields.description: First hint: conceptual nudge. Second: strategy. Last: closest to the solution.

semantics.label: Worked Example
semantics.description: After repeated failed checks, a fully worked solution is offered for study.

fields.label: Enable worked example
fields.description: Reveals the worked example below the task after the configured number of failed checks.

fields.label: Reveal after failed checks
fields.description: Number of failed checks after which the worked example appears.

fields.label: Worked example code
fields.description: The complete solution, ideally with explanatory comments per line.
